slot.brief: Use Λm = Λ°m − K√c type data (or similar) to find molar conductivity at a given concentration.

stem: At 298 K, the molar conductivity at infinite dilution of a strong electrolyte is $390.0 \times 10^{-4}\ \text{S m}^2 \text{mol}^{-1}$ and its Kohlrausch constant is $80.0 \times 10^{-4}\ \text{S m}^2 \text{mol}^{-1} (\text{mol L}^{-1})^{-1/2}$. The molar conductivity of a $0.01\ \text{M}$ solution of this electrolyte is
solution:
For a strong electrolyte, $�\Lambda_m=\Lambda_m^\circ-K\sqrt{c}$.
At $c=0.01\,\text{M}$, $\sqrt{c}=0.1$, so
$$\Lambda_m=(390.0-80.0\times0.1)\times10^{-4}=382.0\times10^{-4}\ \text{S m}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}.$$
